title: Universal Clifford Algebras and Their PBW Basis

items.title: Universal Clifford algebra of a quadratic space

references.title: Jean Gallier, Clifford Algebras, Clifford Groups, and a Generalization of the Quaternions: The Pin and Spin Groups, §1.2
M. F. Atiyah, R. Bott, and A. Shapiro, Clifford Modules, Part I, §1

items.definition:
Let $k$ be a field with $\operatorname{char}(k)\ne2$, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and let $B:V\times V\to k$ be a symmetric bilinear form, not necessarily nondegenerate. Put $Q(v)=B(v,v)$. Write $T_k(V)$ for the tensor algebra and $j:V\to T_k(V)$ for its degree-one inclusion ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]]). For each $v\in V$, set $r_v=j(v)j(v)-Q(v)1$ and let $J_Q$ be the intersection of all two-sided ideals of $T_k(V)$ containing every $r_v$ ([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]]). This family is nonempty because it contains $T_k(V)$, and its intersection is a two-sided ideal; thus $J_Q$ is the smallest such ideal.

Define the **universal Clifford algebra** with the plus-$Q$ convention by

$$\mathrm{Cl}^{+}(V,Q):=T_k(V)/J_Q.$$

The quotient operations are induced from $T_k(V)$; the two-sided ideal condition makes multiplication of cosets well defined. Let $q_Q:T_k(V)\to\mathrm{Cl}^{+}(V,Q)$ be the quotient map, put $i_Q=q_Q\circ j$, and write $\bar v=i_Q(v)$. The defining relation is $\bar v^{\,2}=Q(v)1$. In this pair, $\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)$ abbreviates $\mathrm{Cl}^{+}(V,Q)$ after this sign convention has been fixed. No nondegeneracy assumption is imposed.

items.title: Wedge and contraction operators satisfy the Clifford relations

references.title: Jean Gallier, Clifford Algebras, Clifford Groups, and a Generalization of the Quaternions: The Pin and Spin Groups, §1.2
M. F. Atiyah, R. Bott, and A. Shapiro, Clifford Modules, Part I, §1

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$, let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, and let $B:V\times V\to k$ be symmetric bilinear, possibly degenerate. Set $Q(v)=B(v,v)$ and let $\Lambda V$ be the exterior algebra of the finite free $k$-module $V$ ([[def-exterior-algebra-of-a-finite-free-module]]). Define $\epsilon_v(\omega)=v\wedge\omega$ and, on decomposable wedges,

$$\iota_v(w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge w_r)=\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^{j-1}B(v,w_j)\,w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\widehat{w_j}\wedge\cdots\wedge w_r,$$

with $\iota_v(1)=0$. Then $\iota_v$ is well defined and $k$-linear, and the operators $c(v)=\epsilon_v+\iota_v$ satisfy $c(v)^2=Q(v)I_{\Lambda V}$ for every $v\in V$, where $I_{\Lambda V}$ is the identity map on $\Lambda V$.

items.title: Polarized relations in a Clifford algebra

references.title: Jean Gallier, Clifford Algebras, Clifford Groups, and a Generalization of the Quaternions: The Pin and Spin Groups, §1.2
M. F. Atiyah, R. Bott, and A. Shapiro, Clifford Modules, Part I, §1

items.statement:
Let $k,V,B,Q$ be as in [[def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space]], and let $\bar v=i_Q(v)$. Then

$$\bar v\bar w+\bar w\bar v=2B(v,w)1$$

for all $v,w\in V$.

items.title: Factorization through the Clifford quotient

references.title: Jean Gallier, Clifford Algebras, Clifford Groups, and a Generalization of the Quaternions: The Pin and Spin Groups, §1.2
M. F. Atiyah, R. Bott, and A. Shapiro, Clifford Modules, Part I, §1

items.statement: Let $q_Q:T_k(V)\to\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)$ be the quotient map from [[def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space]]. If $A$ is a unital associative $k$-algebra and $\psi:T_k(V)\to A$ is a unital $k$-algebra homomorphism satisfying $\psi(j(v)^2-Q(v)1)=0$ for every $v\in V$, then there is a unique unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $\bar\psi:\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)\to A$ with $\psi=\bar\psi\circ q_Q$.

items.title: Universal property of the Clifford algebra

references.title: Jean Gallier, Clifford Algebras, Clifford Groups, and a Generalization of the Quaternions: The Pin and Spin Groups, §1.2
M. F. Atiyah, R. Bott, and A. Shapiro, Clifford Modules, Part I, §1

items.statement: Let $k,V,B,Q$ be as in [[def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space]], and let $A$ be a unital associative $k$-algebra. For every $k$-linear map $f:V\to A$ satisfying $f(v)^2=Q(v)1_A$ for all $v\in V$, there is a unique unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $\bar f:\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)\to A$ such that $\bar f\circ i_Q=f$.

items.title: PBW basis and exterior associated graded for a Clifford algebra

references.title: Jean Gallier, Clifford Algebras, Clifford Groups, and a Generalization of the Quaternions: The Pin and Spin Groups, §1.2
M. F. Atiyah, R. Bott, and A. Shapiro, Clifford Modules, Part I, §1

items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$, let $V$ be finite-dimensional of dimension $n$, and let $B$ be any symmetric bilinear form on $V$, possibly degenerate; put $Q(v)=B(v,v)$. Fix an ordered basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$. Then

$$1,\qquad \bar e_{i_1}\cdots\bar e_{i_r}\quad(1\le i_1<\cdots<i_r\le n)$$

is a $k$-basis of $\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)$, so $\dim_k\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)=2^n$. Give $\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)$ the word-length filtration $F_{-1}=0$ and, for $m\ge0$, let $F_m$ be the span of products of at most $m$ canonical generators. The natural graded algebra map

$$\Lambda V\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_F\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)=\bigoplus_{m\ge0}F_m/F_{m-1}$$

that sends $v\in V$ to the degree-one class of $\bar v$ is an isomorphism, where the graded product is induced by $F_pF_q\subseteq F_{p+q}$. No nondegeneracy hypothesis is needed.

title: Universal Clifford Algebras and Their PBW Basis: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A one-dimensional Clifford algebra for any quadratic coefficient
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic not $2$, let $V=ke$ and let $B(e,e)=a\in k$. Then $\mathrm{Cl}(V,Q)$ has basis $1,\bar e$ and multiplication table determined by $\bar e^{\,2}=a1$. This remains true at $a=0$; no matrix classification for $a\ne0$ is asserted.

items.title: The zero quadratic form gives the exterior algebra
items.statement: Let $B=0$ on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ and hence $Q=0$. The two quotient presentations identify $\mathrm{Cl}(V,0)$ canonically with $\Lambda V$. If $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ is an ordered basis, their common basis is $1$ and the increasing square-free monomials. The form is degenerate whenever $V\ne0$.

items.title: A degenerate one-dimensional Clifford algebra need not be semisimple
items.statement: The left regular module of an algebra $A$ is $A$ with action by left multiplication. The false claim is: the left regular module of every finite-dimensional Clifford algebra over a field of characteristic not $2$ is a direct sum of simple left modules. Here “simple” means nonzero with no proper nonzero submodule; “semisimple” for a module means a direct sum of simple submodules.
